title: Mentions: each module lists the prompts that name it
description: A plan, not built: a prompt that names Page is tagged Page, and the Page module lists those prompts. Waits for your yes.

add.text:
**The plan in one line:** each prompt gets a short list of the modules it names, and a module page asks for the prompts that name it, so opening Page shows every ask about Page. **Study only: nothing is built until you say yes.**

**This week's numbers (2026-11-02 to 11-08, 259 of your prompts):** 1 typed a `#Name` or `@Name`, 41 named a module in plain words, 218 named none. So typed tags alone would list almost nothing; the tag has to come from the words.

add.title: What exists: the pieces, but no list per module
add.description: `#Page` already becomes a link, and Refine already picks a module per ask; nothing turns either into "the prompts about Page".
add.text:
- **ext/Mention** (live): turns `#Page` and `@owner` into an icon link. Its two name lists are the vocabulary: `maps/refs.js` (35 names) and `maps/people.js` (10), kept fresh by `Server/plugins/MentionSync.js`.
- **ext/Refine's `RefinedCard`** (live): each refined ask gets a `target` module (`RefinedCard.js:65`). But the browser dictation sessions this week have **0** refined lines, and nothing reads targets back per module.
- **Search terms** sections in the readmes (Item, List, Page, sessions, Servex, Dictate): 79 terms, a ready glossary.
- **`Server/PastWork.mjs`** finds modules by word when you search; it stores no tag.
- **The 2026-10-12 asks-by-module list**: a one-off for 2 modules, dead.

Full table with each caller: [past-work.md](/framework/ai/sessions/2026/11/06/spawned/mastermind-session-truth/mentions-plan/past-work.md)

add.title: Where tags come from: typed, Refine, or a word match
add.description: Typed `#Page` is exact but rare (1 of 259); a plain word match finds 41 but mostly "mastermind"; Refine's target is the best source and does not run on dictation yet.
add.text:
| Source | This week | Good | Bad |
|---|---|---|---|
| **typed** `#Page` / `@owner` | 1 prompt | exact, your choice | you almost never type it |
| **word**: a name from the maps or a Search term, as a whole word | 41 prompts, 47 tags | free, instant | top hit is "mastermind" (21), a role, not a module; "page" said aloud is often a web page (2 found: "the chat V3 page", "load this page") |
| **refine**: Refine's `target` per ask | 0 on dictation | a model read the ask | only where Refine runs |

By source: 223 dictation prompts, 10 VS Code, 26 from the cloud voice record (task titles, since that record keeps no raw owner turn). Top names: mastermind 21, owner 8, Page 3, Servex 2, Item 2. Checked twice: tags summed per prompt = tags summed per name (47 = 47), and my own recount of dictation gave the same 223 prompts and 18 "mastermind" hits.

**Chosen:** every tag records `how` (typed, refine or word). A module page shows typed and refine tags by default, and word tags behind a toggle. Raw numbers: [counts.json](/framework/ai/sessions/2026/11/06/spawned/mastermind-session-truth/mentions-plan/counts.json)

add.title: Where the data lives: computed from the prompts, not a second file
add.description: The tags are worked out by code from the words already logged; a module page asks one query, `page.mentions()`, and never knows which store answered.
add.text:
```js
// node: one class works out the tags from the prompts already logged
Mentions.of("Page")      // → [{prompt, session, at, text, how: "typed" | "refine" | "word"}], newest first
Mentions.in(prompt)      // → [{name: "Page", how: "word"}]

// it is one more query source, the way SessionIndex serves "tasks"
QueryServer.source("mentions", {...})   // Server/SessionIndex.mjs:209 is the model

// browser: any module page
await page.mentions()    // asks the "mentions" source for page.name; store-agnostic
```

**Why computed:** the prompts are the source of truth already (law 7, compute, don't recall). A stored index would be a second copy that drifts when the vocabulary grows.

**Alternative, one index file** (`ai/mentions.jsonl`): faster to read cold and readable on the static site with no server. It wins if module pages must show this on the deployed site; then node writes the file from the same class, and nothing else changes.

**Later, a line on each prompt:** when every channel writes through `Ask.write`, it can store `mentions` on the prompt at write time, so a tag is fixed when said. Today browser dictation does not go through `Ask.write` (found in this study), so that comes after.

add.title: After your yes: three small steps, about $9
add.description: First a node class and its test, with nothing visible changing (~$3); then a Prompts tab on module pages (~$3); then Refine targets for dictation (~$3).
add.text:
1. **`Mentions` class + test** (`core/Session/Mentions.mjs` or beside SessionIndex; the name and home settled first). It reads the three prompt shapes already logged (VS Code `Prompt`, `refined` lines, dictation sentences grouped by `prompt` id), tags each with refs.js, people.js and the readme Search terms, and serves the `mentions` query source. Its check: tags per prompt = tags per name. ~$3
2. **A Prompts tab on a module page**: `page.mentions()` drawn as a list (date, first line, `how` chip, link to the session). First on Page, Item and Servex, the three with the most tags. Shots at 400, 1200, 1920 and 3440. ~$3
3. **Refine targets join in**: read `RefinedCard` `target`s as `how: "refine"` tags, and run Refine over dictation prompts. ~$3

**Risks.** Wrong tags ("page" meaning a web page): every tag shows its `how`, so you can see a weak one. Reading every log on each query: SessionIndex already caches the sessions in memory; reuse it. A vocabulary that misses names: refs.js updates itself, and each new Search terms section adds words.

add.title: What it must not duplicate
add.description: It reuses the Mention name lists, SessionIndex's cache and Refine's targets; it builds no second search and no second vocabulary.
add.text:
- **ext/Mention's maps** stay the one vocabulary: the tagger imports `refs.js` and `people.js`, never a copy.
- **SessionIndex** stays the one in-memory index of the sessions: `mentions` is one more query source beside `tasks`, not a second loader.
- **PastWork** stays the search; it can use tags to rank, later.
- **Sessions** keep the prompts; the tagger only reads them.
- **Refine** keeps picking targets with a model; the tagger reads them and never asks a model again.

add.title: The alternatives
add.description: Typed tags only (lists almost nothing today), or a model tags every prompt (best recall, about $0.50 a week, slower).
add.text:
- **Typed tags only** (`#Page`): exact, but 1 of 259 prompts had one this week. Wins only if you start typing or saying tags.
- **A model tags every prompt** (Haiku): reads meaning, so "this page" is not tagged Page. Roughly $0.002 a prompt, about $0.50 a week at this week's 259. Wins if word tags prove too noisy after step 2; it would slot in as a fourth `how`.
- **One stored index file**: see the card above; wins for the static site.
